newsitem.title: USA: San Diego County, Calif., ratings cut to new low.
newsitem.headline: San Diego County, Calif., ratings cut to new low.

text.p: Moody's Investors Service Inc on Thursday cut San Diego County's debt ratings to an all-time low, warning that the Southern California county's fiscal flexibility and credit position had weakened.
Bill Kelly, San Diego County's assistant auditor-controller, said Moody's move was likely to increase the county's borrowing costs next year.

"We're disappointed in the action taken by Moody's but understand the pressure they're under in rating counties whose flexibility has been limited by actions of the state," Kelly said after the Moody's announcement.

Kelly said the downgrade would modestly increase the county's borrowing costs when it issued tax and revenue anticipation notes next May. That note issue was expected to total about $250 million, he said. To reduce its borrowing costs,the county was now more likely to use bond insurance and other forms of credit enhancement, he said.

"The convergence of fiscal pressures, from state revenue reductions and the lingering effects of the recession, coupled with unique problems related to the county's solid waste system and investment pool, has strained the county's fiscal flexibility and weakened its credit position," Moody's said.
Moody's said the downgrade also reflected factors common to all California counties, including limits on revenues and the added burden associated with new federal welfare reform.

Moody's lowered San Diego County long-term obligations to Baa1 from single-A. Baa1, considered a medium grade rating, is a single notch below single-A, an upper-medium grade rating. Baa1 is several steps below the highest rating of AAA.
The Baa1 rating was a new low for these obligations.

"I don't think any further action is imminent," said Moody's Vice President Nikolai Sklaroff. But he added that Moody's would continue to monitor the situation. "This is a situation that hasn't reached its final resolution."
